Neon's Free plan currently allows **100 projects**, with **100 CU-hours of compute per project per month**. The sources disagree on storage and on one compute figure, so check the current pricing page before relying on either.

- **Storage:** Neon's own blog post says the limit rose to 1 GB per project, with existing projects getting the increase automatically (Database storage on the Neon Free plan is now 1 GB per project, up from 0.5 GB.). Older Neon FAQ and pricing pages still list 0.5 GB (Free plan quotas (100 CU-hours, 0.5 GB) are per project).
- **Compute:** The Free plan can autoscale up to 2 CU (Computes scale to zero after 5 minutes of inactivity and can scale up to 2 CU (≈8 GB RAM) when active.). One plans page gives a lower figure of 50 CU-hours per project (Includes 10 projects, 50 CU-hours/project, 0.5 GB storage per branch, and 5 GB of egress.), which conflicts with the 100 figure elsewhere.
- **Branches:** Each project gets 10 branches on Free, and extra branches are not available on that plan (Extra branches are not available on the Free plan.).
- **Egress:** Public network transfer is 5 GB per project per month (includes 100 projects, 10 branches per project, 100 CU-hours of compute per project per month, 0.5 GB of storage per project, and 5 GB of public network transfer per project per month.).
- **Over limits:** Compute is suspended when CU-hours run out, and storage above the cap suspends the project rather than billing for it (Storage above 0.5 GB: the project is suspended rather than billed. Delete data or upgrade to continue writing.). Suspension does not delete data.

The official Supabase pricing page is the most authoritative source here, and it lists the free tier as follows:

- **Database, users, egress:** The free tier includes 500 MB database size, 50,000 monthly active users, and 5 GB egress plus 5 GB cached egress. (Get started with unlimited API requests, 50,000 monthly active users, 500 MB database size, 5 GB egress, 5 GB cached egress, 1 GB file storage)
- **Project cap:** Free accounts are limited to 2 active projects. (Limit of 2 active projects.)
- **Pausing:** Free projects pause after a week without activity. Data is kept, but you must resume the project manually. (Free plan projects are paused automatically after 7 days of inactivity. Your data is retained, but the project goes offline until you manually resume it.)

Pro-tier figures for comparison: 8 GB disk per project, 250 GB egress, and 100,000 MAUs, with overage rates billed beyond those. (Everything in the Free Plan, plus 100,000 monthly active users then $0.00325 per MAU, 8 GB disk size per project then $0.125 per GB, 250 GB egress then $0.09 per GB) Pro also keeps projects running rather than pausing them. (It has increased resource limits and removes the inactivity pause.)

Discrepancy to note: several third-party guides list free file storage as 500 MB, while the official page says 1 GB. I'd treat the official page as the source of truth, but it's worth confirming on the live pricing page.

content.text:
## Free tier comparison for Postgres: Neon, Supabase and PlanetScale

I couldn't open the vendors' pages directly. Fetching them failed with a proxy error, so these numbers come from web-search summaries. Treat them as unverified until you've checked the live pricing pages.

| | **Neon Free** | **Supabase Free** | **PlanetScale** |
|---|---|---|---|
| Free tier? | Yes | Yes | **No free tier found.** Cheapest is a paid plan. |
| Storage | 1 GB per project (older pages say 0.5 GB) | 500 MB database, 1 GB file storage | n/a |
| Compute | 100 CU-hours per project per month (one page says 50), autoscaling up to 2 CU (about 8 GB RAM) | Not covered in my results | n/a |
| Projects | 100 | 2 active | n/a |
| Branches | 10 per project | Not covered in my results | n/a |
| Egress | 5 GB per project per month | 5 GB, plus 5 GB cached | n/a |
| Idle behavior | Scales to zero after 5 minutes idle | Project pauses after 7 days of inactivity, and you resume it manually | n/a |
| Other | When limits run out, compute or the project is suspended rather than billed, and data is kept | 50,000 monthly active users, unlimited API requests | Cheapest Postgres is a single-node plan at $5/month. High-availability (HA) plans cost more, for example about $30/month for PS-10 HA. |

### Where each number comes from
- **Neon:**
  - The [Neon free plan limits FAQ](https://neon.com/faqs/free-plan-limits-and-quotas) gives 100 projects, 10 branches, 100 CU-hours, 5 GB egress, scale-to-zero after 5 minutes, and suspension instead of billing.
  - The [Neon blog post](https://neon.com/blog/neon-free-plan-1-gb-per-project) says storage rose to 1 GB per project.
  - The conflicting 0.5 GB figure is on older Neon pages, and the 50 CU-hours and 10 projects figure is on one plans page. Both look outdated, but I couldn't confirm that.
  - Related pages: [Neon plans docs](https://neon.com/docs/introduction/plans), [pricing](https://neon.com/pricing).
- **Supabase:**
  - The [official pricing page](https://supabase.com/pricing.md) gives 500 MB database, 50,000 monthly active users, 5 GB egress plus 5 GB cached, 1 GB file storage, 2 active projects, and the 7-day inactivity pause.
  - Some third-party guides list 500 MB of file storage instead. I went with the official page.
- **PlanetScale:**
  - A [Bytebase comparison](https://www.bytebase.com/blog/postgres-hosting-options-pricing-comparison/) and other third-party sources say the free Hobby plan was removed in April 2024 and not brought back.
  - The same sources give the $5/month single-node Postgres plan, introduced October 30, 2025, and the HA pricing.
  - One [CostBench page](https://costbench.com/software/database-as-service/planetscale/free-plan/) claims a free plan exists as of June 2026. A later CostBench page says there isn't one, and the other sources agree, so I treat that claim as an outlier.

### Takeaway
- **Neon** is the most generous for hobby work: many projects, branching, and scale-to-zero. Its limits are enforced per project.
- **Supabase** gives a smaller database (500 MB) and only 2 projects, but it bundles auth, file storage and APIs. The 7-day pause is the main catch.
- **PlanetScale** has no free option for Postgres, so budget at least $5/month.

Before you rely on any of this, check each live pricing page, especially Neon's storage and compute figures and whether PlanetScale has added a free plan.

Sources:
- [Neon free plan limits FAQ](https://neon.com/faqs/free-plan-limits-and-quotas)
- [Neon storage blog post](https://neon.com/blog/neon-free-plan-1-gb-per-project)
- [Neon plans docs](https://neon.com/docs/introduction/plans)
- [Neon pricing](https://neon.com/pricing)
- [Supabase pricing](https://supabase.com/pricing.md)
- [Bytebase: Postgres hosting pricing comparison](https://www.bytebase.com/blog/postgres-hosting-options-pricing-comparison/)
- [CostBench: PlanetScale free plan](https://costbench.com/software/database-as-service/planetscale/free-plan/)
